finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") but discards its boolean return value, so any authenticated user can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: Any logged-in User u reaching POST /tenants/{t}/wipe, plus the attacker-chosen tenant path parameter.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 (destructive, irreversible tenant wipe).

trace.note: void wipe(User u, String tenant) accepts caller and target tenant.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") is called; return value ignored.
requireRole only returns u.roles().contains(role) and never throws (javadoc line 13 confirms).

finding.guards_checked: requireRole (boolean predicate, result ignored, no enforcement); checkRole (throwing variant, not used in wipe); no tenant-ownership check against u; no caller-side check visible in this file.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) is a boolean predicate that never throws, and its result is discarded at src/Admin.java:26, so it enforces nothing. checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) is the throwing variant but is not called in wipe(). No tenant-ownership check exists in wipe(), and the directory contains only src/Admin.java, so no caller-side check is visible.
verdict.reason: wipe() at src/Admin.java:26 discards the boolean from requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16), so repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 runs for any caller holding any user record, which is an authenticated low-privilege user as the candidate states.

finding.claim: export() checks for the OWNER role globally, not scoped to the target tenant, so an OWNER of one tenant may export another tenant's data if roles are not tenant-scoped.
finding.source: A logged-in User u whose roles set contains "OWNER" for some tenant, plus an attacker-chosen tenant path parameter.

trace.note: void export(User u, String tenant) accepts caller and target tenant.
checkRole(u, "OWNER") passes if OWNER appears anywhere in u.roles().
repo.export(tenant) runs without comparing tenant to any tenant bound to u.
User record has no tenant identifier, so the role cannot be scoped to a tenant in this code.

finding.guards_checked: checkRole (throwing, enforces role presence but not tenant scope); User record has no tenant field; no tenant-ownership check in export. Confidence depends on whether roles are per-tenant or a global platform role, which is not visible in this file.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) throws SecurityException when OWNER is absent, so it enforces role presence only. No tenant-ownership check exists in export (src/Admin.java:31-33). The User record (src/Admin.java:4) has no tenant field.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: checkRole at src/Admin.java:32 is a real throwing check, and repo.export(tenant) at line 33 runs with no tenant comparison. Whether this is exploitable depends on whether the roles Set in User (src/Admin.java:4) is populated per-tenant, and the only file in the directory is Admin.java, so that cannot be decided here.
